notSuppressed_expresslyConsidered.ruling: NOT SUPPRESSED. Law-3 EXCEPTION applies: this is a NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun, not obvious harm and not owner malice. PhusdStableMinter offers three superficially interchangeable stand-down levers - pause(), setStablecoinEnabled(stable,false) and updateExchangeRate(stable,0). The first two REVERT inside minter.mint and unwind the annihilation whole (the project's own test_pausedMinterRollsEverythingBack at :265 proves it). The third reverts nowhere and settles lossily, taking the caller's entire stablecoin half for the antimatter half alone. NOTHING in the code, the NatSpec or the interface distinguishes them. Test applied: would a competent, NON-MALICIOUS owner be surprised by this consequence? YES. Also note a malicious owner has strictly BETTER levers than this one - which is itself proof the finding is not a malicious-owner vector.

titleAndMechanismRewriteREQUIRED.storedTitleIsArithmeticallyWRONG: 'A near-zero exchangeRate turns a soft throttle into a hard brick: the stable leg rounds to zero...'
titleAndMechanismRewriteREQUIRED.refutation: REFUTED BY TIER 3 (INV-B). mintedForStable == amount*R/1e18 EXACTLY for every registered decimals value - the decimal adjustment cancels. It is zero only when amount*R < 1e18; for amount = 100e18 that means R < 0.01 wei, and R is a uint256, so at that size the stable leg is zero ONLY at R == 0 exactly. There is NO near-zero band. Counterexamples: 18-dec R=1 wei amount=100e18 -> 100 wei not 0; 6-dec R=1e15 amount=100e18 -> 0.1e18 not 0. This ALSO refutes CODE-003's inherited claim of a 1e16 cliff.
titleAndMechanismRewriteREQUIRED.proposedCorrectedTitle: At exchangeRate == 0 (or amount*R < 1e18) the stable leg mints zero and, with the protocol-side zero guard deleted, the annihilation now SETTLES silently: the caller's whole stablecoin half is consumed into the yield strategy with no redeem path and only the antimatter half is delivered - a ~50% shortfall against the documented 2x, with Annihilated emitted as if normal. Between those endpoints the shortfall is CONTINUOUS at amount*(1e18-R)/1e18, which no zero check can see.
titleAndMechanismRewriteREQUIRED.instruction: Whoever applies this must NOT re-argue it on a near-zero rounding band. Argue it on R == 0 exactly (or the amount*R < 1e18 dust case) and on the continuous partial shortfall.
